summary: Independently confirmed all 6 prior reviews' findings are real, and found a new CRITICAL, unlisted regression: suspendTenant() re-enters getState()/applyOverrideAndEscalation() before its own UPDATE runs, causing unbounded recursion (stack overflow, request 500s, and the tenant permanently stuck unable to ever persist as suspended) for any payment_grace/read_only tenant that crosses the suspend threshold -- triggerable by a single ordinary HTTP request through BillingEnforcementGuard or by DunningService's daily sweep, no concurrency required. Also confirmed getState() is a genuine CQS-violating query-with-side-effect (though traced its write is conditional on real threshold crossings, not an unconditional per-request UPDATE -- that specific framing is refuted), found 2 additional legacy tenants.active readers (leads.service.ts public registration check, autentique.service.ts webhook) beyond the ones already catalogued, and found the dunning dedup-key comment is inaccurate (updated_at is bumped by idempotent re-entrant writes in suspendTenant/startPaymentGrace, not only on real transitions). None of this is fixed; must not ship.
